messages:
maria (PM): heads up — FinSight just pinged our AE with a P0 request. they want a 2x throughput SLA for their peak inference workloads next quarter and ask if we can move that up. they say revenue + pilot hinge on this.

sara (AE): cc @maria. i confirmed it's tied to a board review in 6 weeks. they cannot postpone. they're willing to sign a dedicated capacity commitment if we can meet the perf numbers.

jon (Eng Lead): quick thoughts — 2x throughput has two surface areas: runtime kernel / batching improvements and dedicated capacity plumbing (autoscale, qps routing). runtime team could target a ~20% perf uplift in 6w, not 2x. infra can provide reserved capacity but cost goes up.

kevin (Infra): infra caveat: we can reserve additional GPUs in Dedicated but that increases monthly commit and pushes queuing changes. also need to update router fallback to disabled for this customer until rollout complete.

li (Design): UX note — if we change routing/fallback, we should add a small in-app banner and a telemetry flag so customer can opt into degraded mode for cost reasons. not a big design lift.

maria (PM): thanks. i sketched 3 options:
A) Full scope shift: pause Q2 non-critical work (embeddings-cost-tune, docs refresh) and dedicate cycles to hit 2x for FinSight — high customer revenue, high risk to other OKRs.
B) Fast-path limited: implement dedicated capacity + routing tweaks for FinSight only, add ops guardrails, push runtime perf improvements as incremental follow-ups. lower risk, partial win.
C) Sales-first: sign commitment for Dedicated, deliver current perf baseline + aggressive billing credits; revisit perf in next quarter.

jon (Eng Lead): technical feasibility ranking: B > C > A. B lets infra isolate customer and buy time for deep kernel work. A is unrealistic without major hiring.

oliver (Finance): number check — if they sign a 12-month dedicated commit at 5x baseline spend we get good NRR but margin hit if we overprovision. need hourly burn forecast. sara can you get a ballpark commit number?

sara (AE): asking them now, expect reply by EOD. preliminary: they can do a 9-12 month commit if we guarantee the perf or credits.

kevin (Infra): ops considerations for B: need a short runbook, rate-limiter override for that customer, and a telemetry flag. estimate: 2 sprint infra change + 1 sprint ops-runbook.

jon (Eng Lead): runtime changes for B: route-level KV cache warmup, affinity packing for FinSight requests, and conservative kernel tweaks. estimate 2 engineers 6 weeks.

maria (PM): OKR impact proposal: move 30% of the "latency & batching" KR to a cross-functional "FinSight priority" lift under customer-driven work. reduce the "embeddings-cost-tune" KR scope by 40%. this preserves top-level velocity. who signs off?

oliver (Finance): need written reforecast to update expected committed ARR and OpEx. if product approves, i'll update the deck for exec.

li (Design): can support banner + telemetry in 1 sprint if engineers can allocate a half-sprint for integration.

jon (Eng Lead): i'm ok with Option B if Product commits to the scope swap and we get the sales commit before we change routing.

maria (PM): proposal motion: approve Option B (fast-path limited) with immediate reforecast and OKR scope-shift as described. action items: 1) sara to confirm commit by EOD (sales). 2) jon/kevin to create infra/runtime tickets with estimates by tomorrow. 3) oliver to draft reforecast. 4) li to queue UX banner. 5) maria to update OKR sheet: https://redwood.app/okrs (link)

ops-bot: scheduled incident runbook created: https://ops.redwood/runbooks/finsight-dedicated (auto)
thread_text_snippet: FinSight P0 throughput ask — team discussion of options (A/B/C), technical estimates, OKR scope tradeoffs, and action items
